# Architecture at a Glance 🗂️

#### Course: Brick Breaker with JavaScript

## Architecture at a Glance 🗂️

The project has two files with a clear boundary between them.

entities.js defines what things are and how they behave on their own. The Ball knows how to move, bounce, and draw itself. The Paddle knows how to respond to input and clamp its position. The Brick knows whether it is alive and how to draw itself.

game.js coordinates everything. It owns the loop, the state machine, the collision checks, and the HUD updates. It does not care how the ball draws itself. It just calls ball.draw(ctx) and trusts the ball to handle it.

That boundary, entities own their own behavior and a coordinator owns their relationships, is a pattern that appears everywhere. You will see it in React components, in backend service layers, and in every game codebase at every scale. The tools change. The separation does not.
